artifact: Reference-tier registry -- the frozen evidentiary content of the reference-tier gate (check_reference_tier.py).
purpose: Every COMPLETED 3D case classified by its REFERENCE STRENGTH (a different axis from the geometric building-block tier in validation_tiers.json). No demo page or credential entry may show a case ABOVE its tier here; a bounded-agreement case always shows its band; a caveated case always shows its caveat; an excluded 2D/axisymmetric case never appears in a 3D listing.
provenance: Sanaa 2026-09-09 (direct): reference-tier credibility standard; every completed 3D case classified by reference strength BEFORE any page shows it; nothing shown above its true tier; a GATE binding demo/credential pages.
frozen: This file is the gate's evidentiary content and is sha-frozen before grading (rule 2). The tier of each case is fixed BEFORE any page is scanned, so a page cannot pick the tier that flatters it. Edits after freeze land only as dated addenda that cannot alter a tier, band or caveat.
authored_by: verification lab-lane (working-tree draft; supervisor diff-reads, plant-drives and commits)

tier_definitions.experiment-validated: Validated against EXPERIMENTAL data; every deviation DISCLOSED.
tier_definitions.bounded-agreement: Agrees within an EXPLICITLY-STATED quantitative band vs a named reference; the band is always shown.
tier_definitions.code-verified: Reproduces a CODE reference only (another solver / a tutorial baseline). NEVER shown as experiment-validated; carries an explicit disavowal.
tier_definitions.method-verified: Internal verification only, no external reference (adjoint FD-verified / primal-converged / bug-find). States its time-box or bug-find; carries an explicit disavowal.

detector.comment: A page's CLAIM about a case is read heuristically from a bounded window (paragraph/block, or one JSON object's strings). A tier above method-verified is only CLAIMED when an ASSERTION CUE co-occurs with a reference token and is NOT negated -- a generic description of what a reference body is does not, by itself, assert that OUR result was validated. This keeps honest 'no wind-tunnel data / self-consistency, not validation' disavowals from reading as claims.
detector._assertion_cues_note: Deliberately excludes the generic 'matches'/'matches the' -- it fires on geometric-hierarchy boilerplate ('the published measurement matches the solved conditions') that asserts nothing about our result. A tier above method-verified is only CLAIMED when one of these result-comparison cues co-occurs with a non-negated reference token.
